text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal met on Monday with Serbian opposition leader Vesna Pesic and said Norway would support the democratic prosess in Serbia. Pesic was invited to Norway by the Helsingfors Committee.
-Norway could lose gas sales worth billions of crowns when Britain starts selling natural gas to continental Europe via the new Interconnector pipeline.
-The government is preparing for the launch of the single European currency, the euro. The euro's consequences for the Norwegian crown will be presented in the revised national budget in the spring.

-Two brokerage houses Orkla Finans and Sundal Collier bought large quantities of shares in Norway's largest insurer Storebrand last week. Orkla and Sundal contacted more than 50 investors to ask them to sell their shares.
-Carbon dioxide emissions from Norwegian oil and gas production will increase to 11.5 million tonnes in 1999, 20 percent more than government estimates.
